subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 42-year-old woman has an asymptomatic 2-cm liver lesion found incidentally on abdominal imaging. It is described as a venous malformation and is the most common benign liver tumor.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Focal nodular hyperplasia
Hepatic adenoma
Cavernous hemangioma
Hepatocellular carcinoma
Hepatic angiosarcoma

explanation_correct: Hepatic hemangioma (cavernous hemangioma) is the most common benign liver tumor, a venous malformation typically occurring at age 30–50 years. It is usually asymptomatic and detected incidentally. Biopsy is contraindicated because of the risk of hemorrhage.

explanation_incorrect.A: Focal nodular hyperplasia is the second most common benign liver tumor, occurs in women aged 35–50, and has a central stellate scar rather than a venous malformation.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hepatic adenoma is a rare benign tumor linked to oral contraceptive or anabolic steroid use that may rupture and cause shock.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hepatocellular carcinoma is the most common primary malignant liver tumor in adults, associated with cirrhosis, HBV, and aflatoxin.
explanation_incorrect.E: Hepatic angiosarcoma is a rare malignant endothelial tumor associated with arsenic and vinyl chloride exposure.

educationalObjective: Cavernous hemangioma is the most common benign liver tumor and a venous malformation; biopsy is contraindicated due to hemorrhage risk.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 40-year-old woman has an incidental liver lesion on CT performed for abdominal pain. Imaging demonstrates a central stellate scar. She takes no oral contraceptives.
question: Which of the following best describes this lesion?

options.text: Most common benign liver tumor with a risk of hemorrhage on biopsy
Rare benign tumor that may rupture, associated with anabolic steroid use
Malignant endothelial tumor associated with arsenic exposure
Most common malignant liver tumor overall, usually multiple
Hyperplastic reaction of hepatocytes to an aberrant dystrophic artery, with a central stellate scar

explanation_correct: Focal nodular hyperplasia is the second most common benign liver tumor and occurs predominantly in females aged 35–50 years. It is a hyperplastic reaction of hepatocytes to an aberrant dystrophic artery and is marked by a central stellate scar. It is usually asymptomatic and detected incidentally.

explanation_incorrect.A: Cavernous hemangioma is the most common benign liver tumor and a venous malformation whose biopsy risks hemorrhage, but it lacks a central stellate scar.
explanation_incorrect.B: Hepatic adenoma is associated with oral contraceptive or anabolic steroid use and can rupture with abdominal pain and shock, not a central scar.
explanation_incorrect.C: Hepatic angiosarcoma is a malignant endothelial tumor associated with arsenic or vinyl chloride exposure.
explanation_incorrect.D: Metastases are the most common malignant liver tumors overall and are rarely solitary; they are not benign hyperplastic lesions.

educationalObjective: Focal nodular hyperplasia is the second most common benign liver tumor, seen in women 35–50, with a central stellate scar from an aberrant artery.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 29-year-old woman who has used oral contraceptives for 8 years presents with sudden severe right upper quadrant pain and hypotension. Imaging shows a ruptured liver lesion with intra-abdominal bleeding.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Hepatic adenoma
Hepatic hemangioma
Focal nodular hyperplasia
Hepatic angiosarcoma
Metastatic breast cancer

explanation_correct: Hepatic adenoma is a rare benign tumor often related to oral contraceptive or anabolic steroid use. It may regress spontaneously or rupture, causing abdominal pain and shock, as in this patient. This distinguishes it from focal nodular hyperplasia (central stellate scar, not hormone related) and hemangioma (biopsy contraindicated because of bleeding risk).

explanation_incorrect.B: Hepatic hemangioma is a venous malformation that is usually asymptomatic and incidental; rupture with shock is not its typical behavior.
explanation_incorrect.C: Focal nodular hyperplasia is often an incidental lesion with a central stellate scar and is not characterized by rupture and shock.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hepatic angiosarcoma is a rare malignant endothelial tumor associated with arsenic or vinyl chloride, not oral contraceptive use.
explanation_incorrect.E: Metastases from breast cancer are usually multiple, rarely solitary, and are not linked to oral contraceptive use.

educationalObjective: Hepatic adenoma is an oral-contraceptive/anabolic-steroid–associated benign tumor that can rupture and cause abdominal pain and shock.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 58-year-old man with cirrhosis from chronic hepatitis C develops anorexia, jaundice, and tender hepatomegaly. A liver mass is found and serum AFP is elevated.
question: Which of the following statements about this patient's mass is most accurate?

options.text: Metastases are the most common primary malignant liver tumor in adults
Hepatocellular carcinoma is the most common primary malignant liver tumor in adults and is associated with all causes of cirrhosis
Hepatic adenoma is the most common primary malignant liver tumor and may rupture
Hepatic angiosarcoma is the most common primary liver malignancy and is linked to aflatoxin
Focal nodular hyperplasia frequently degenerates into hepatocellular carcinoma

explanation_correct: Hepatocellular carcinoma (hepatoma) is the most common primary malignant liver tumor in adults. It is associated with HBV (with or without cirrhosis), all other causes of cirrhosis (HCV, alcoholic and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, autoimmune disease, hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency), and carcinogens such as aflatoxin from Aspergillus. Findings include anorexia, jaundice, and tender hepatomegaly; it may cause decompensation of stable cirrhosis and portal vein thrombosis and spreads hematogenously.

explanation_incorrect.A: Metastases are the most common malignant liver tumors overall, but they are not primary liver tumors; HCC is the most common primary malignant tumor in adults.
explanation_incorrect.C: Hepatic adenoma is a rare benign tumor, not a primary malignancy, although it can rupture and cause shock.
explanation_incorrect.D: Hepatic angiosarcoma is a rare malignant endothelial tumor linked to arsenic and vinyl chloride; aflatoxin is associated with HCC.
explanation_incorrect.E: Focal nodular hyperplasia is a benign hyperplastic reaction to an aberrant artery and is not a precursor to HCC.

educationalObjective: HCC is the most common primary malignant liver tumor in adults, linked to HBV, all cirrhosis etiologies, and aflatoxin.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 62-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis is enrolled in a liver cancer surveillance program. A new 3-cm hepatic lesion is detected on ultrasound and confirmed with contrast-enhanced MRI.
question: Which of the following is most appropriate for monitoring recurrence after treatment?

options.text: Repeat liver biopsy every 3 months
Serum alkaline phosphatase
Serum bilirubin alone
Serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)
Serum gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase

explanation_correct: Hepatocellular carcinoma is screened for with ultrasound and confirmed with contrast CT or MRI; biopsy is reserved for cases in which the diagnosis is uncertain. Recurrence is monitored with serum AFP. HCC may lead to decompensation of previously stable cirrhosis (eg, ascites) and portal vein thrombosis, and it spreads hematogenously.

explanation_incorrect.A: Liver biopsy is used if the diagnosis is uncertain, not for routine recurrence surveillance after a confirmed lesion.
explanation_incorrect.B: Alkaline phosphatase reflects cholestasis or biliary disease and is not a marker for HCC recurrence.
explanation_incorrect.C: Bilirubin is a general marker of liver disease and hemolysis rather than tumor recurrence.
explanation_incorrect.E: GGT rises in various liver and biliary diseases and with alcohol use, but it is not used to monitor HCC recurrence.

educationalObjective: HCC surveillance uses ultrasound, contrast CT/MRI confirms the diagnosis, and serum AFP monitors recurrence.

subject: Gastrointestinal
vignette: A 67-year-old man with a history of colorectal cancer presents with multiple liver lesions on CT. He has no cirrhosis and a normal serum AFP.
question: Which of the following best characterizes these lesions?

options.text: They are most likely hepatic adenomas related to prior anabolic steroid use
They represent focal nodular hyperplasia with central stellate scars
They are hepatic hemangiomas, which are venous malformations
Metastases are the most common malignant liver tumors overall, often from GI, breast, or lung primaries, and are rarely solitary
They are hepatocellular carcinoma arising in a noncirrhotic liver with elevated AFP

explanation_correct: Metastases are the most common malignant liver tumors overall; primary sources include GI, breast, and lung cancers, and metastases are rarely solitary. This patient's known colorectal primary with multiple lesions and no cirrhosis fits best. HCC is the most common primary malignant liver tumor in adults, usually arises in cirrhosis, and is monitored with AFP; hemangioma, focal nodular hyperplasia, and adenoma are benign tumors.

explanation_incorrect.A: Hepatic adenomas are rare benign lesions linked to oral contraceptive or anabolic steroid use, not multiple lesions in a patient with known colorectal cancer.
explanation_incorrect.B: Focal nodular hyperplasia is a benign hyperplastic lesion with a central stellate scar, typically a single incidental finding in women.
explanation_incorrect.C: Hemangiomas are benign venous malformations and the most common benign liver tumor, not malignant deposits.
explanation_incorrect.E: HCC would typically arise in cirrhosis and be associated with elevated AFP; this patient has neither cirrhosis nor an elevated AFP.

educationalObjective: Metastases are the most common malignant liver tumors overall (GI, breast, lung primaries) and are rarely solitary.
